storylines.label: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash
storylines.latest_title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash vs V4 Pro vs V4-Flash: 4.4x Gap [2026]

prior_narrative.tldr: DeepSeek shipped V4.1-Flash on Sep 10, claiming it beats flagship V4-Pro while cutting the memory agents need to run it. The efficiency claim rattled Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron shares within a day, and DeepSeek quantified it Sep 13 as a 75% HBM and 87.5% SSD cut.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Third-party host ZenMux added DeepSeek V4.1-Flash for high-throughput reasoning on Sep 22, the first sign the model is spreading to inference platforms beyond DeepSeek's own API.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Anyone calling the V4-Pro endpoint is now served different weights than they pinned, at a price that keeps falling, without a version bump to signal either change -- and now a third-party host serves the same model, so routing choices need re-checking too.

status.state: Shipped · V4-Pro traffic silently rerouted, now on third-party hosts too
status.detail: V4.1-Flash launched Sep 10 beating V4-Pro on quality while cutting agent memory needs; the efficiency claim rattled memory-chip stocks by Sep 11, and by Sep 14 DeepSeek was routing all V4-Pro traffic to V4.1-Flash at a price that kept falling. A Sep 20 follow-up added the 1M-context/KV-compression specifics behind the architecture, and by Sep 22 third-party host ZenMux was serving the model too.

beats.headline: Pricing pressure builds as reviewers call the architecture a bigger leap than a point release
beats.summary: A Sep 17 benchmark puts the coding gap at 11 points over Qwen3-Coder and Devstral, and a Sep 20 follow-up from a second outlet adds concrete numbers behind the causal encoder-decoder design: a 1M-token context window via extreme KV-cache compression.

DeepSeek quietly swaps V4-Pro traffic for V4.1-Flash at Flash pricing
beats.summary: Four days after launch, calls to the V4-Pro endpoint are served by V4.1-Flash instead, billed at the cheaper Flash rate.

Cached-input pricing drops again to $0.003 per million tokens
ZenMux adds V4.1-Flash for high-throughput reasoning
beats.summary: First sign the model is spreading to inference platforms beyond DeepSeek's own API.

open_questions: Does the claimed memory-footprint cut hold up in independent agent-workload benchmarks, not just DeepSeek's own numbers?
Will DeepSeek formally deprecate the V4-Pro endpoint, or keep serving V4.1-Flash under the old name indefinitely?
Do outputs from the V4-Pro endpoint show measurable quality or behavior differences now that V4.1-Flash serves them?
Has the 1M-token context and KV-cache compression figure been independently benchmarked, or does it restate DeepSeek's own claims?
Does ZenMux serve the identical weights and config as DeepSeek's own endpoint, or a re-quantized variant with different behavior?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Re-run your eval suite against the V4-Pro endpoint: you're getting V4.1-Flash's outputs at a still-falling price, and any prompt or behavior tuned to V4-Pro specifically may have silently drifted. If you route through ZenMux or another third-party host, verify it serves the same weights before trusting cross-provider evals.

storylines.latest_title: What a task costs on Opus 5.5 / claude.dev Blog

prior_narrative.tldr: Anthropic answered Zhipu's GLM-5.3-Flash price undercut with a 75% cache-price cut on Fable/Mythos 5.1 in early September. On Sep 22 Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI answered within about an hour with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, turning the pricing skirmish into a same-day flagship race.
prior_narrative.whats_new: By Sep 23, AINews reported the Opus 5.5 launch triggered board-wide 40-50% price cuts across labs, while Opus 5.5 also reached AWS Bedrock with new per-task cost guidance.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Whatever Claude-vs-GPT cost model you pinned evals to last week is now stale -- Opus 5.5's AWS availability and the wider 40-50% price cuts change per-token math across both labs.

status.detail: Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol/Luna's same-day launch escalated into board-wide 40-50% price cuts by Sep 23, with Opus 5.5 now live on AWS Bedrock.

Which labs specifically matched the 40-50% cut, and does actual per-task cost (per AWS's guidance) net out cheaper despite Opus 5.5's higher list price?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Re-run your Claude vs. GPT cost model against Opus 5.5's AWS Bedrock pricing and the newly-cut competitor rates -- don't assume last week's per-token numbers still hold.
